questions.question:
Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if

they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the

Statements:

All pages are diaries.

Some diaries are books.

All books are notebooks.

Conclusions:

I. No page is a notebook.

II. All pages are notebooks.

III. All diaries being notebooks is a possibility.

options.A: Both conclusion I and II follow
options.B: Only conclusions I and III follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

[Image: https://storage.googleapis.com/tb-img/production/25/04/IMG%20-%20637%20%2029-04-25%20%20%20Yuvraj%20kori%201.png]

Conclusions:

I. No page is a notebook → Does not follow (As all pages are diaries, some diaries are books and all books are notebooks. As no direct relation is given between pages and notebooks, therefore it is false.)

II. All pages are notebooks → Does not follow (As all pages are diaries, some diaries are books and all books are notebooks. So it is possible but not definite.)

III. All diaries being notebooks is a possibility → Follow (As some diaries are books and all books are notebooks. As statement restricts whole diaries from being books therefore it is possible and thus is true.)

∴ Here, Only conclusion III follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

questions.question: What is net investment?

options.A: Sum of all the investments in a country

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Gross investment - depreciation.

📌 📌 Key Points

A company's net investment is the sum of its expenditures on capital assets less the cost of depreciating those assets.

This gives an idea of the actual spending on durable products utilized by the company in its operations, such as buildings, machinery, and software.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Depreciation: It means a fall in the value of an asset because of usage or with efflux of time or due to obsolescence or accident.

Appreciation: It means an increase in the value of an asset over time. This the opposite of depreciation. It is an upward adjustment of the value of an asset held on a company's accounting book.

Deceleration: It is the rate at which an asset's value in the market goes down.

Gross investment: It is the total amount spent on goods in order to produce other goods and services.

Net investment: It is the amount of increase in productive stock.

Capital investment is the money used by a business to purchase fixed assets, such as land, machinery, or buildings. The money may be in the form of cash, assets, or loans. Without capital investment, businesses may have a hard time getting off the ground.

questions.question: Microbes like Rhizobium, Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter are used for:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is nitrogen cycling.

📌 📌 Key Points

Nitrogen Cycle-

Nitrogen is an essential constituent of protein and is a basic building block of all living tissue. It constitutes nearly 16% by weight of all the proteins that is, converted to ammonia, nitrites or nitrates before it can be taken up by plants.

Nitrogen fixation on earth is accomplished in three different ways:

a) By microorganisms (bacteria and blue-green algae)

b) By man using industrial processes (fertilizer factories) and

c) To a limited extent by atmospheric phenomena such as thunder and lighting

Certain microorganisms are capable of fixing atmospheric nitrogen into ammonium ions. These include free-living nitrifying bacteria (e.g. aerobic Azotobacter and anaerobic Clostridium) and symbiotic nitrifying bacteria living in association with leguminous plants and symbiotic bacteria living in non-leguminous root nodule plants (e.g. Rhizobium) as well as blue-green algae (e.g. Anabaena, Spirulina).

Ammonium ions can be directly taken up as a source of nitrogen by some plants, or are oxidized to nitrites or nitrates by two groups of specialised bacteria: Nitrosomonas bacteria promote the transformation of ammonia into nitrite. Nitrite is then further transformed into nitrate by the bacteria Nitrobacter.

The nitrates synthesised by bacteria in the soil are taken up by plants and converted into amino acids, which are the building blocks of proteins. These then go through higher trophic levels of the ecosystem. During excretion and upon the death of all organisms nitrogen is returned to the soil in the form of ammonia.

Certain quantities of soil nitrates, being highly soluble in water, are lost to the system by being transported away by surface run-off or groundwater. In the soil as well as oceans there are special denitrifying bacteria (e.g. Pseudomonas), which convert the nitrates/nitrites to elemental nitrogen. This nitrogen escapes into the atmosphere, thus completing the cycle.

The periodic thunderstorms convert the gaseous nitrogen in the atmosphere to ammonia and nitrates which eventually reach the earth’s surface through precipitation and then into the soil to be utilized by plants.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Carbon Cycle

The carbon cycle involves several processes, including photosynthesis, respiration, decomposition, and combustion. Plants absorb carbon dioxide (CO₂) during photosynthesis, while animals release CO₂ through respiration.

Carbon is stored in various reservoirs, including the atmosphere (as CO₂), oceans (as dissolved CO₂ and organic carbon), soil (as organic matter), and living organisms. These reservoirs play a crucial role in regulating global climate.

Human activities, such as fossil fuel combustion and deforestation, significantly alter the carbon cycle by increasing atmospheric CO₂ levels, contributing to global warming and climate change.​

Water Cycle-

The hydrologic cycle is the continuous circulation of water in the Earth-atmosphere system which is driven by solar energy. Water on our planet is stored in major reservoirs like atmosphere, oceans, lakes, rivers, soils, glaciers, snowfields, and groundwater. Water moves from one reservoir to another by the processes of evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation, deposition, runoff, infiltration, and groundwater flow.

Water as an important ecological factor determines the structure and function of the ecosystem. Cycling of all other nutrients is also dependent upon water as it provides their transportation during the various steps. It acts as a solvent medium for their uptake of nutrients by organisms.

Sulphur Cycle-

The sulphur reservoir is in the soil and sediments where it is locked in organic (coal, oil and peat) and inorganic deposits (pyrite rock and sulphur rock) in the form of sulphates, sulphides and organic sulphur.

It is released by weathering of rocks, erosional runoff and decomposition of organic matter and is carried to terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems in a salt solution.

The sulphur cycle is mostly sedimentary except two of its compounds hydrogen sulphide (H2S) and sulphur dioxide (SO2) add a gaseous component to its normal sedimentary cycle.

Sulphur enters the atmosphere from several sources like volcanic eruptions, combustion of fossil fuels, from the surface of the ocean and from gases released by decomposition. Atmospheric hydrogen sulphide also gets oxidised into sulphur dioxide.

Atmospheric sulphur dioxide is carried back to the earth after being dissolved in rainwater as weak sulphuric acid.

Monera kingdom:

Fungi kingdom:

Bryophytes

Gymnosperms and

Angiosperms

Gymnosperms

Gymnosperms are vascular plants having naked seeds.

Angiosperms

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides that 'there shall be a Vice President of India'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Article 63.

📌 📌 Key Points

Article 63

Article 63 of the Indian Constitution states that "There shall be a vice president of India."

The vice president acts as president in the absence of the president due to death, resignation, impeachment, or other situations.

The vice president of India is also ex officio chairperson of the Rajya Sabha. When a bill is introduced in Rajya Sabha, the vice president decides whether it is a financial bill or not.

If he is of the opinion, a bill introduced in the Rajya Sabha is a money bill, he would refer the case to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha for deciding it.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Article 61

The process for the impeachment of the President is outlined in Article 61 of the Indian Constitution.

Either House of Parliament may file the impeachment accusations.

The President must be notified 14 days in advance, and these allegations must be signed by one-fourth of the House members who framed them.

The other House, which is tasked with conducting an investigation into the allegations, receives the impeachment resolution when it has been approved by a two-thirds majority of the entire membership of that House.

The President has the right to show up and be represented during such an investigation.

The President is removed from office as of the date the resolution is passed if the other House concurs with the accusations and approves the impeachment resolution with a two-thirds majority of its members.

Impeachment is a quasi-judicial process in Parliament as a result.

In this context, it is important to keep in mind two things:

nominated members of either House of Parliament may take part in the impeachment of the President even though they did not cast a ballot in his election;

and elected members of state legislative assemblies and the union territories of Delhi and Puducherry may not, even though they cast a ballot in the President's election.

Article 65

Article 65 deals with the Vice-President acting as President or discharging the functions of the President in the event of a vacancy.

​Article 62

Article 62 of the Indian Constitution deals with the time frame for holding an election to fill a vacancy in the office of the President.

The correct answer is 131.9.

📌 📌 Key Points

The green revolution is the rise in agricultural productivity, particularly in developing nations, made possible by the use of novel crops and farming techniques.

Given that he started the Green Revolution in India, M. S. Swaminathan is regarded as its father. He was motivated by Norman Borlaug's effort.

Norman Borlaug started the Green Revolution movement in the 1960s. He is referred to as the "Father of the Green Revolution" globally. For his efforts in creating High Yielding Varieties (HYVs) of wheat, it resulted in him being awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.

In order to enhance food production and reduce hunger and poverty, high-yielding cultivars of rice and wheat were first introduced in India in the 1960s.

In Punjab, the Green Revolution in India was first implemented in late 1966 or early 1967 as a part of a development initiative launched by international donor organisations and the Indian government.

One of the innovative techniques created during the Green Revolution was drip irrigation. This technology allowed water to drop slowly and steadily to the roots of plants, saving water and promoting more sustainable agriculture.

India has achieved significant progress thanks to the Green Revolution, which has brought about a previously unheard-of level of food security. It has helped many non-poor people avoid the poverty and hunger they would have otherwise faced while lifting a significant number of poor people out of poverty

questions.question: Calculate the oxidation number of 'S' in H2S2O7.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 6.

📌 📌 Key Points

Let's denote the oxidation number of sulfur as 'x'.

In H₂S₂O₇:

Hydrogen (H) has an oxidation number of +1.

Oxygen (O) has an oxidation number of -2.

The overall charge of the molecule is 0.

So, we can set up the equation:

2(+1) + 2(x) + 7(-2) = 0

Simplifying:

2 + 2x - 14 = 0

2x = 12

x = +6

Therefore, the oxidation number of sulfur (S) in H₂S₂O₇ is +6.

questions.question: Which digits should come in place * and $,respectively, if the number 72864*$ is divisible by both 8 and 5?
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

For a number to be divisible by 5, its last digit ($) must be 0 or 5.

For a number to be divisible by 8, it must be an even number, so $ must be 0.

The last three digits (4*0) must be divisible by 8.

Checking the given options, if * = 4, the number 440 is divisible by 8 (440 ÷ 8 = 55).

∴ The correct answer is 4 and 0.

Alternate Method

Given:

Number = 72864*$

The number is perfectly divisible by both 8 and 5.

Concept Used:

Divisibility by 5: The unit digit must be 0 or 5.

Divisibility by 8: The number formed by the last three digits must be divisible by 8.

Calculation:

⇒ For the number to be divisible by 5, the unit digit $ can be 0 or 5.

⇒ For the number to be divisible by 8, it must be an even number. Hence, $ cannot be 5.

⇒ ∴ $ = 0

⇒ The last three digits form the number 4*0.

⇒ Now, we check the given options for *.

⇒ If * = 4, the number formed is 440. Since 440 ÷ 8 = 55, it is completely divisible by 8.

⇒ If * = 2, the number formed is 420. Since 420 ÷ 8 = 52.5, it is not completely divisible by 8.

⇒ ∴ The missing digits are * = 4 and $ = 0.

∴ The correct answer is 4 and 0.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Divisibility Rule of 3 & 9

A number is divisible by 3 or 9 if the sum of all its digits is completely divisible by 3 or 9, respectively.

Divisibility Rule of 4 & 8

A number is divisible by 4 if its last two digits are divisible by 4. It is divisible by 8 if its last three digits are divisible by 8.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of its digits at odd places and the sum of its digits at even places is either 0 or a multiple of 11.

In ΔPQR, the perpendicular PS divides the triangle into two right-angled triangles sharing the same altitude PS.

Using the property of shared altitude: PS2 = PQ2 − QS2 and PS2 = PR2 − SR2.

Equating both expressions gives: PQ2 − QS2 = PR2 − SR2

questions.question: The incomes of P, Q and R are in the ratio 10 : 12 : 9 and their expenditures are in the ratio 12 : 15 : 8. If Q saves 25% of his income, then what is the ratio of the savings of P, Q and R?
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

Q saves 25% of his income, which means Q's expenditure is 75% of his income.

Ratio of Q's Expenditure to Income = 75% = 3 / 4 ⇒ 15y / 12x = 3 / 4.

This gives y / x = (3 / 4) × (12 / 15) = 3 / 5 ⇒ x / y = 5 / 3. Let x = 5 and y = 3.

Savings = Income − Expenditure ⇒ P = (10×5 − 12×3), Q = (12×5 − 15×3), R = (9×5 − 8×3).

Savings Ratio = (50 − 36) : (60 − 45) : (45 − 24) = 14 : 15 : 21.

∴ The correct answer is 14 : 15 : 21.

Alternate Method

Given:

Income ratio of P, Q, R = 10 : 12 : 9

Expenditure ratio of P, Q, R = 12 : 15 : 8

Savings of Q = 25% of Q's income

[Image: https://cdn.testbook.com/temp_9b074215fed048d0a74db7c63c6da372.png/1777717345.png]

Formula Used:

Savings = Income − Expenditure

Calculations:

⇒ Let the incomes of P, Q, and R be 10x, 12x, and 9x respectively.

⇒ Let the expenditures of P, Q, and R be 12y, 15y, and 8y respectively.

⇒ Q's saving = Q's income − Q's expenditure

⇒ Q's saving = 12x − 15y

⇒ It is given that Q saves 25% of his income:

⇒ 12x − 15y = 25% of 12x

⇒ 12x − 15y = (25 / 100) × 12x

⇒ 12x − 15y = 3x

⇒ 9x = 15y ⇒ y = (9 / 15)x = (3 / 5)x

⇒ Now substituting y = 3x / 5 to find savings of all three:

⇒ Saving of P = 10x − 12y = 10x − 12 × (3x / 5) = 10x − 36x / 5 = 14x / 5

⇒ Saving of Q = 12x − 15y = 12x − 15 × (3x / 5) = 12x − 9x = 3x = 15x / 5

⇒ Saving of R = 9x − 8y = 9x − 8 × (3x / 5) = 9x − 24x / 5 = 21x / 5

⇒ Ratio of savings = 14x / 5 : 15x / 5 : 21x / 5

⇒ Ratio = 14 : 15 : 21

∴ The correct answer is 14 : 15 : 21.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Income, Expenditure & Savings

The fundamental relation is Income = Expenditure + Savings. If income and expenditure are given in separate ratios, using independent variables for each helps to find the relationship between them via any given connecting condition.

Ratio Multipliers

A ratio a : b implies actual values are ax and bx where x is a common multiplier. When two different groups of quantities are in ratios, they require two different variables (e.g., x and y).

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

Converting percentages to fractions (like 25% = 1/4) simplifies calculation involving equations. Thus, 25% savings implies 75% (or 3/4) of income is expenditure.

questions.question: In triangles ABC and DEF, AB = FD and ∠A = ∠D. The two triangles are congruent by SAS criterion if:
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

The SAS (Side-Angle-Side) criterion requires two sides and the included angle of one triangle to be equal to the corresponding parts of the other.

We are given Side AB = FD and Included Angle ∠A = ∠D.

The second side forming ∠A in ΔABC is AC, and the second side forming ∠D in ΔDEF is DE.

Thus, for the triangles to be congruent by SAS, these second sides must necessarily be equal.

∴ The correct answer is AC = DE.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ In ΔABC and ΔDEF:

⇒ AB = FD (Side)

⇒ ∠A = ∠D (Included Angle)

Concept Used:

⇒ According to the SAS (Side-Angle-Side) congruence rule, two triangles are congruent if two sides and the included angle of one triangle are equal to the corresponding two sides and the included angle of the other triangle.

A

Required: AC = DE for SAS Congruence

Calculations:

⇒ In ΔABC, the angle ∠A is strictly formed by the intersection of sides AB and AC.

⇒ In ΔDEF, the corresponding angle ∠D is strictly formed by the intersection of sides FD and DE.

⇒ Since we already have AB = FD and the included angle ∠A = ∠D, the other pair of sides forming these equal angles must also be equivalent to satisfy the SAS criteria.

⇒ Therefore, the side AC of ΔABC must be exactly equal to the side DE of ΔDEF.

⇒ AC = DE

∴ The correct answer is AC = DE.

📌 📌 Additional Information

SSS (Side-Side-Side) Congruence

If all three sides of one triangle are structurally equal to the corresponding three sides of another triangle, then the triangles are fully congruent.

ASA (Angle-Side-Angle) Congruence

If two angles and the included side between them in one triangle are equal to the corresponding parts of another triangle, then the triangles are congruent.

AAS (Angle-Angle-Side) Congruence

If two adjacent angles and a non-included side of one triangle are equal to the corresponding consecutive angles and side of another triangle, they are congruent.

RHS (Right angle-Hypotenuse-Side) Congruence

If in two right-angled triangles, the hypotenuse and one standard side of one triangle are identical to the hypotenuse and corresponding side of the other, they are congruent.

questions.question: Two pipes, A and B, can fill a tank in 10 minutes and 20 minutes, respectively. The pipe C can empty the tank in 30 minutes. All the three pipes are opened at a time in the beginning. However, pipe C is closed 2 minutes before the tank is filled. In what time, will the tank be full (in minutes)?
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

Total work capacity = LCM(10, 20, 30) = 60 units.

Efficiencies of pipes A, B, and C are +6, +3, and −2 units/min respectively.

If outlet pipe C remained open for the last 2 minutes, it would empty 2 × 2 = 4 units.

Effective total work if all three pipes worked for the entire time = 60 − 4 = 56 units.

Total time = Effective total work ÷ Net efficiency = 56 ÷ (6 + 3 − 2) = 8 minutes.

∴ The correct answer is 8 minutes.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by pipe A to fill the tank = 10 minutes

Time taken by pipe B to fill the tank = 20 minutes

Time taken by pipe C to empty the tank = 30 minutes

| Pipe | Time (mins) | Total Work | Efficiency |
| A | 10 | 60 | +6 |
| B | 20 | +3 |
| C | 30 | −2 |

Calculations:

⇒ Let the total time taken to fill the tank be x minutes.

⇒ Pipes A and B are open for the entire duration, so they work for x minutes.

⇒ Pipe C is closed 2 minutes before the tank is filled, so it works for (x − 2) minutes.

⇒ Work done by A + Work done by B + Work done by C = Total Work

⇒ 6x + 3x − 2(x − 2) = 60

⇒ 9x − 2x + 4 = 60

⇒ 7x = 56

⇒ x = 8

∴ The correct answer is 8 minutes.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

Pipes that fill the tank are assigned positive efficiency, while pipes that empty the tank are assigned negative efficiency. Net Efficiency = Sum of all active efficiencies.

Leaving Before Completion

If a worker (or pipe) stops working 'n' units of time before completion, add their potential work for those 'n' units to the total work, and assume everyone worked until the end. For outlet pipes, this means subtracting the work since they possess negative efficiency.

LCM Method for Time & Work

Assuming the total work as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the given individual times avoids fractional calculations and significantly increases speed in competitive exams.

questions.question: A payment of ₹120 is made with ₹10, ₹5 and ₹2 coins. A total of 25 coins are used. Which of the following is the number of ₹10 coins used in the payment?
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

Assume all 25 coins are of the lowest denomination (₹2). Base value = 25 × 2 = ₹50.

Extra amount to be matched to reach ₹120 = 120 − 50 = ₹70.

Each ₹10 coin adds ₹8 extra, and each ₹5 coin adds ₹3 extra compared to a ₹2 coin. Let their numbers be x and y.

This forms the equation: 8x + 3y = 70.

Checking the options for x: If x = 8, then 8(8) + 3y = 70 ⇒ 64 + 3y = 70 ⇒ 3y = 6 ⇒ y = 2 (Valid integer).

∴ The correct answer is 8 coins.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total number of coins used = 25

Total payment made = ₹120

Let the number of ₹10 coins be x, ₹5 coins be y, and ₹2 coins be z.

Equations:

⇒ x + y + z = 25 ... (i)

⇒ 10x + 5y + 2z = 120 ... (ii)

[Image: https://cdn.testbook.com/temp_446c95e78e72490fb2063a3c17b92974.png/1777701722.png]

Calculations:

⇒ Multiply equation (i) by 2:

⇒ 2x + 2y + 2z = 50 ... (iii)

⇒ Subtract equation (iii) from equation (ii) to eliminate z:

⇒ (10x + 5y + 2z) − (2x + 2y + 2z) = 120 − 50

⇒ 8x + 3y = 70

⇒ Since x and y must be positive integers, let's test the given options for the value of x:

⇒ Option 1: x = 6 ⇒ 48 + 3y = 70 ⇒ 3y = 22 (Not an integer)

⇒ Option 2: x = 4 ⇒ 32 + 3y = 70 ⇒ 3y = 38 (Not an integer)

⇒ Option 3: x = 10 ⇒ 80 + 3y = 70 ⇒ 3y = −10 (Not possible as count cannot be negative)

⇒ Option 4: x = 8 ⇒ 64 + 3y = 70 ⇒ 3y = 6 ⇒ y = 2 (Valid integer)

⇒ Substitute x = 8 and y = 2 in equation (i) to find z:

⇒ 8 + 2 + z = 25 ⇒ z = 15.

⇒ Cross-verifying the total value: (8 × 10) + (2 × 5) + (15 × 2) = 80 + 10 + 30 = ₹120.

∴ The correct answer is 8 coins.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Diophantine Equations

A linear equation of the form ax + by = c where only integer solutions are expected. When counting physical objects like coins, the variables must strictly be non-negative integers.

Elimination Method

A structured algebraic technique to solve simultaneous equations by multiplying with constants to equalize the coefficients of one variable, and then subtracting equations to eliminate it.

Average Denomination Rule

The overall average value of each coin provides a good estimation point. Here, Average = Total Amount ÷ Total Coins = 120 ÷ 25 = ₹4.8, which helps logic check your final ratio.

questions.question: If 28.9 : x :: x : 36.1, and x > 0, then find the value of x.
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

For a continuous proportion a : x :: x : b, the mean proportional x = √(a × b).

⇒ x = √(28.9 × 36.1)

⇒ x = √(289/10 × 361/10)

⇒ x = (17 × 19) ÷ 10

⇒ x = 323 ÷ 10 = 32.3

∴ The correct answer is 32.3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Proportion: 28.9 : x :: x : 36.1

Condition: x > 0

Formula Used:

In a proportion a : b :: c : d, the product of the means equals the product of the extremes (a × d = b × c).

[Image: https://cdn.testbook.com/temp_b94288528b19437986f4d79b4c8b7e6a.png/1777717366.png]

Calculations:

⇒ x × x = 28.9 × 36.1

⇒ x2 = (289 ÷ 10) × (361 ÷ 10)

⇒ x = √((289 × 361) ÷ 100)

Since x > 0, we take the positive square root:

⇒ x = (√289 × √361) ÷ √100

⇒ x = (17 × 19) ÷ 10

⇒ x = 323 ÷ 10 = 32.3

∴ The correct answer is 32.3.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Mean Proportional

If three quantities a, b, and c are in continued proportion (a : b = b : c), then the middle term b is called the mean proportional between a and c, given by the formula b = √(a × c).

Third Proportional

If a : b = b : c, then c is the third proportional to a and b, calculated by the rule c = b2 ÷ a.

Fourth Proportional

If four quantities a, b, c, and d are in proportion (a : b = c : d), then d is the fourth proportional to a, b, and c, defined by d = (b × c) ÷ a.

questions.question: The height of a cylinder is 20 cm. The lateral surface area is 1760 cm2. Its volume is:
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

The volume formula includes π (22/7), meaning the final volume must perfectly be divisible by 11.

Check the given options for the divisibility rule of 11 (difference between the sum of alternating digits must be 0 or a multiple of 11).

Among the given options, only 12320 satisfies this condition: (1 + 3 + 0) − (2 + 2) = 4 − 4 = 0.

∴ The correct answer is 12320 cm3.

Alternate Method

[Image: https://cdn.testbook.com/temp_e37ae913ec3a45e2a5e4f84253b47b51.png/1777642636.png]

Given:

Height of cylinder (h) = 20 cm

Lateral Surface Area (LSA) = 1760 cm2

Formula Used:

LSA = 2πrh

Volume = πr2h

Calculations:

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r × 20 = 1760

⇒ 880/7 × r = 1760

⇒ r = (1760 × 7) ÷ 880

⇒ r = 14 cm

Now, finding the volume using the radius:

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 14 × 14 × 20

⇒ Volume = 22 × 2 × 14 × 20

⇒ Volume = 44 × 280

⇒ Volume = 12320 cm3

⇒ Alternatively, Volume = (LSA ÷ 2) × r = (1760 ÷ 2) × 14 = 880 × 14 = 12320 cm3

∴ The correct answer is 12320 cm3.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

The total surface area includes the lateral area plus the two circular bases. Formula: TSA = 2πrh + 2πr2 = 2πr(h + r).

Volume of a Cone

A cone with the same base radius and height as a cylinder has exactly one-third of the cylinder's volume. Formula: Volume = (1/3)πr2h.

Volume of a Hollow Cylinder

For a hollow cylindrical pipe with outer radius R and inner radius r, the material volume is given by V = π(R2 − r2)h.

questions.question:
Raj divides ₹1,200 in the ratio 2 : 1 : 3 among three of his friends. The amount equal to the sum of three times the largest share and two times the smallest share is:

Ans
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

Total ratio parts = 2 + 1 + 3 = 6 parts.

Value of 1 part = 1200 ÷ 6 = ₹200.

Required expression = 3 × (Largest Ratio Part) + 2 × (Smallest Ratio Part).

Required parts = 3 × 3 + 2 × 1 = 9 + 2 = 11 parts.

Required amount = 11 × 200 = ₹2,200.

∴ The correct answer is ₹2,200.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total amount to be divided = ₹1,200

Ratio of shares among three friends = 2 : 1 : 3

[Image: https://cdn.testbook.com/temp_cb39950280d24be1af22726465ef8fa6.png/1777717306.png]

Calculations:

⇒ Sum of all ratio parts = 2 + 1 + 3 = 6 parts

⇒ Value of 6 parts = ₹1,200

⇒ Value of 1 part = 1200 ÷ 6 = ₹200

⇒ Smallest share (1 part) = ₹200

⇒ Largest share (3 parts) = 3 × 200 = ₹600

⇒ Amount to find = 3 × Largest share + 2 × Smallest share

questions.question: The average of 12 numbers is 48. The average of the first 5 numbers is 45 and the average of next 4 numbers is 52. If the 10th number is 10 less than the 11th number and is 5 more than the 12th number, then the average of the 11th and 12th numbers is:

📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

Net deviation of the first 9 numbers from the average (48) = 5 × (45 − 48) + 4 × (52 − 48) = −15 + 16 = +1

Sum of 10th, 11th, and 12th numbers = (3 × 48) − 1 = 143

Let the 12th number = x, then 10th = x + 5, and 11th = x + 15

Sum = x + 5 + x + 15 + x = 3x + 20 = 143 ⇒ x = 41

11th number = 41 + 15 = 56, and 12th number = 41. Average = (56 + 41) ÷ 2 = 48.5

∴ The correct answer is 48.5.

Alternate Method

⇒ Sum of the first 5 numbers = 5 × 45 = 225

⇒ Sum of the next 4 numbers = 4 × 52 = 208

⇒ Sum of 10th, 11th, and 12th numbers = 576 − (225 + 208) = 143

⇒ Let the 12th number be x.

⇒ The 10th number is 5 more than the 12th number ⇒ 10th number = x + 5

⇒ The 10th number is 10 less than the 11th number ⇒ 11th number = (x + 5) + 10 = x + 15

⇒ Sum of the last 3 numbers = (x + 5) + (x + 15) + x = 143

⇒ 3x = 123 ⇒ x = 41

⇒ 11th number = 41 + 15 = 56

⇒ 12th number = 41

⇒ Average of the 11th and 12th numbers = (56 + 41) ÷ 2 = 97 ÷ 2 = 48.5

∴ The correct answer is 48.5.

📌 📌 Additional Information

questions.question:
Find the value of the following expression.

\(\sqrt{\frac{1 + \sin \theta}{1 - \sin \theta}}\)
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

Multiply inside the root by the conjugate of the denominator: (1 + sin θ).

The denominator becomes 1 − sin2 θ = cos2 θ.

The numerator becomes (1 + sin θ)2.

Taking the square root gives (1 + sin θ) ÷ cos θ.

Splitting the terms gives (1 ÷ cos θ) + (sin θ ÷ cos θ) = sec θ + tan θ.

∴ The correct answer is sec θ + tan θ.

Alternate Method

Given:

Expression: √[ (1 + sin θ) ÷ (1 − sin θ) ]

Formulas Used:

1 − sin2 θ = cos2 θ

sec θ = 1 ÷ cos θ

tan θ = sin θ ÷ cos θ

Calculations:

⇒ √[ (1 + sin θ) ÷ (1 − sin θ) ]

Rationalise the denominator by multiplying the numerator and the denominator by (1 + sin θ):

⇒ √[ { (1 + sin θ) × (1 + sin θ) } ÷ { (1 − sin θ) × (1 + sin θ) } ]

⇒ √[ (1 + sin θ)2 ÷ (1 − sin2 θ) ]

⇒ √[ (1 + sin θ)2 ÷ cos2 θ ]

Removing the square root:

⇒ (1 + sin θ) ÷ cos θ

Distributing the denominator:

⇒ (1 ÷ cos θ) + (sin θ ÷ cos θ)

⇒ sec θ + tan θ

∴ The correct answer is sec θ + tan θ.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Standard Trigonometric Results

√[(1 − sin θ) ÷ (1 + sin θ)] = sec θ − tan θ

Cosine Equivalent Results

√[(1 + cos θ) ÷ (1 − cos θ)] = cosec θ + cot θ

Pythagorean Identities

sin2 θ + cos2 θ = 1 | sec2 θ − tan2 θ = 1 | cosec2 θ − cot2 θ = 1

Rationalisation Strategy

For square roots of trigonometric fractions (like 1 ± sin θ), multiplying by the conjugate of the denominator easily converts the expression into a perfect square, allowing direct simplification.

questions.question: M and N walk along a circular track. They start at 5:00 a.m. from the same point in the opposite directions. M and N walk at a speed of 5 rounds per hour and 2 rounds per hour, respectively. How many times will they cross each other before 6.30 a.m. on the same day?
questions.solution:
📌 📌 Shortcut Trick

When bodies move in opposite directions on a circular track, they cross each other at a frequency equal to the sum of their speeds in rounds per unit time.

Relative speed = 5 + 2 = 7 rounds per hour.

This means they cross each other 7 times every hour.

Total time from 5:00 a.m. to 6:30 a.m. = 1.5 hours.

Total crossings = 7 × 1.5 = 10.5 crossings.

∴ The correct answer is 10 times.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of M = 5 rounds/hr

Speed of N = 2 rounds/hr

Time interval = 5:00 a.m. to 6:30 a.m. = 1.5 hours

Formula Used:

Total Crossings = Relative Speed × Total Time

Calculation:

[Image: https://cdn.testbook.com/temp_a1a8bbd95f56465689b192285228735d.png/1777718559.png]
⇒ Relative speed = 5 + 2 = 7 rounds/hr

⇒ This means M and N jointly cover 7 complete laps of the track in 1 hour.

⇒ Hence, they cross each other 7 times in 1 hour.

⇒ In 1.5 hours, relative laps completed = 7 × 1.5 = 10.5 laps.

⇒ Since a crossing occurs for every fully completed relative lap, we take the integer value.

⇒ Number of times they completely cross each other = 10

∴ The correct answer is 10 times.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Meetings in Opposite Directions

When moving in opposite directions, the frequency of meetings per unit time is the sum of their individual speeds (rounds per unit time): S1 + S2.

Meetings in Same Direction

When moving in the same direction, the frequency of meetings per unit time is the difference of their individual speeds: |S1 − S2|.

Meeting at the Starting Point

Regardless of the direction, the time taken to meet for the first time at the starting point is the LCM of the individual times taken by each person to complete one full round.

questions.question: If x + 1/x = 15, then the value of (7x2 - 9x + 7) / (x2 - x + 1) is:

Divide the numerator and the denominator by x to simplify.

Take x common from both the numerator and the denominator.

⇒ Numerator = x[7x − 9 + 7/x] = x[7(x + 1/x) − 9]

⇒ Denominator = x[x − 1 + 1/x] = x[(x + 1/x) − 1]

Cancel out x from both the numerator and the denominator.

⇒ Value = [7(x + 1/x) − 9] / [(x + 1/x) − 1]

Now, substitute x + 1/x = 15 into the equation.

⇒ Value = (7 × 15 − 9) / (15 − 1)

⇒ Value = (105 − 9) / 14

⇒ Value = 96 / 14

⇒ Value = 48 / 7

∴ The correct answer is 48/7.

questions.question: The measures of the three angles of a triangle are in the ratio 17 : 13 : 15. Find the positive difference between the greatest and the smallest of these three angles.
questions.solution:

Total parts of the angles = 17 + 13 + 15 = 45 parts.

We know the sum of the interior angles of a triangle is always 180°.

45 parts = 180° ⇒ 1 part = 4°.

Difference between greatest (17) and smallest (13) angle parts = 17 − 13 = 4 parts.

Difference in degrees = 4 parts × 4° = 16°.

∴ The correct answer is 16°.

questions.question: A certain sum of money becomes seven times itself when invested at a certain rate of simple interest, in 14 years. How much time (in years, rounded off to 2 decimal places) will it take to become 18 times itself at the same rate?

questions.question:

options.B: Bananas have not been liked by Sonam.
options.C: Bananas are not liked by Sonam.
options.D: Bananas had not been liked by Sonam.

questions.correct_answer: Bananas are not liked by Sonam.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.

📌 📌 Key Points

Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.

In the active voice, the sentence is: "Sonam does not like bananas."

To convert to passive voice: Place the object "bananas" at the beginning.

Change the active verb form "does not like" to "are not liked" (present simple passive).

Ensure the subject "Sonam" remains, but the focus is on the object "bananas."

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Correct Sentence: "Bananas are not liked by Sonam."

📌 📌 Additional Information

Option 1: "Banana is not liked by Sonam." – Incorrect, as "banana" is singular instead of the plural "bananas."

Option 2: "Bananas have not been liked by Sonam." – Incorrect tense (present perfect passive).

Option 4: "Bananas had not been liked by Sonam." – Incorrect tense (past perfect passive).

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. The genuine beliefs, though not unconsciously acquired by most children; and even if they depart from these beliefs in later life

B. Something of them remains deeply implanted, ready to emerge in a time of stress of crisis

C. The importance of education in forming character and opinion is very great and well recognised by all

D. Education is, as a rule, the strongest force on the side of what exists and again fundamental change
questions.solution:

📌 📌 Key Points

Next, part A, this sentence connects to C by elaborating on the influence of education in forming beliefs in children. It builds on the idea of how education shapes these beliefs, even if the beliefs may not last forever.

Part B following A, this sentence explains how even if beliefs formed during education are altered over time, a part of them remains ingrained, ready to resurface during challenging situations.

Finally, part D concludes by discussing the significant role education plays in maintaining existing beliefs, which supports the overall argument of the paragraph.

Therefore, the correct answer is CABD.

📌 📌 Additional Information

Option 1 (DCAB): This option starts with “Education is, as a rule, the strongest force,” which disrupts the logical flow of the paragraph.

Option 2 (DABC): This option also begins with part D, which does not smoothly lead into the other sentences.
